one_month_reasoning: Window 2026-10-02 to 2026-10-31. Scheduled: September production/operations update (~mid-October, as August's came 2026-09-17), which will show hashrate (~80+ EH/s self-mining) and BTC output; with hashprice up from ~$28 to ~$40/PH/day in September it should read decently but it is largely known. Q3 results are expected around mid-November (outside the window). No lock-up or index event identified. The main driver is BTC beta (BTC ~$83.5k) and possible further ATM/financing news (new $1B shelf, Tydal ~$500M project financing pending), which skews slightly negative; 25-30% short interest adds squeeze risk the other way. I therefore stay near a symmetric lognormal: median $10.50 (slight downward tilt for dilution overhang), monthly sigma ~30% (108%/3.5).

fair_value.method: Blend of DCF ($2.27, 30%), SOTP ($7.75, 40%) and EV/NTM sales 3.0x ($8.16, 30%) = $6.23. All methods deduct ~$1.35B of current net debt (converts + 13%-cost related-party loans + BTC loan, less cash) growing to ~$1.75B with 12 months of burn; the equity is a thin slice on top of a leveraged, mostly-mining EV.

bear.story: BTC slides toward $65-70k, hashprice back below $30 and BTDR's all-in cost (~$90k/BTC) leaves mining cash-negative after interest; Tydal slips or project financing comes on bad terms; more converts/ATM at lower prices and the $373M current BIT related-party loans get rolled at 13%. Market starts discounting the April-2028 halving. Equity rerated to ~1.5x sales after dilution.

base.story: Tydal phases come online Q4-26 to H2-27 roughly on time, hashprice holds high-$30s, AI cloud grows modestly; but ongoing capex and refinancing keep dilution flowing (share count up ~10-15%) and the halving looms. Stock trades near the blended fair value plus some optionality on the 3 GW power portfolio.

bull.story: BTC rallies above $110k and a second large HPC lease (Rockdale/Clarington) is signed with an investment-grade tenant; market rerates BTDR toward contracted-HPC peers (12.9x EV/NTM sales), short covering from ~25-30% of float amplifies the move toward the ~$22 consensus target.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$5 (under the Feb-2026 direct offering at $7.94 and the Aug-2026 insider buys at $8.84-9.04, and roughly where equity is worth only Tydal net of debt), the stock would most likely be signalling a fundamental problem rather than noise: failed or punitive Tydal project financing, a Volta/tenant problem, inability to roll the 13% related-party loans, or a distressed equity raise. At that level my base case (orderly but dilutive funding) is broken.

reasoning: Facts: Q2-26 revenue $228.8M (+47%), gross loss $8.5M, net loss $92.3M, adj. EBITDA $31.1M; H1 operating cash flow -$505M and capex $360M; ~$1.2B of converts plus ~$730M of related-party BIT Group loans (13% effective on the asset loans, 3,669 BTC borrowed) against ~$250M estimated cash. CoinShares puts BTDR's all-in cost at $89.7k/BTC versus BTC ~$83.5k today, and the 10Y Treasury is 5.29%, which makes long-duration, cash-burning equity expensive. The bull case is real (Tydal $4.7B/16-yr lease at ~90% NOI, AI cloud ARR $86M, ~3 GW power, consensus PT ~$22, CFO/CSO open-market buys near $9, 25-30% short interest), but every dollar of it sits behind leverage and a long pipe of dilution (converts at $9.93-$17.77, $1B shelf, Tydal's $500M build). My DCF of contracted+existing cash flows gives only ~$2/share because 2027 FCFF is about -$460M and terminal FCF is ~$340M at a 12.5% WACC; SOTP ($7.75) and EV/sales at BTDR's own ~3x ($8.16) give more credit to Tydal and the power portfolio. Blended fair value ~$6.2. Bear-lane findings (Callisto governance allegations from 2025, the SEAL04 class action, KBW's $10 target citing inventory, cash burn and related-party debt, Needham's pipeline cut) are mostly known to the market, so I do not treat them as an imminent collapse. I set the 12-month distribution as a lognormal with median $8.60 (between fair value and spot, reflecting expected dilution and halving overhang but also ongoing AI-optionality pricing) and sigma 0.80 (somewhat below 108% realized vol), giving P(>=$10.64) ~40% and ~7% tail below $2.66 for financing distress. Scenario mean (~$10.25) is a bit below spot. Research limits: Twelve Data and Alpha Vantage endpoints were paywalled/rate-limited, so consensus estimates came from web aggregators; Simply Wall St and some sites blocked fetching, and the Basis Report article's date/context is inconsistent (insider buy itself corroborated by a second source).
